newsitem.title: FRANCE: France fails to withdraw anti-Clinton charge.
newsitem.headline: France fails to withdraw anti-Clinton charge.

text.p: France failed on Wednesday to withdraw a minister's comment that an Africa tour by U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher was aimed at promoting President Bill Clinton's re-election campaign.

The State Department had on Tuesday demanded that France withdraw a remark by junior cooperation minister Jacques Godfrain that he was "delighted to see (Clinton) showing interest in Africa and making it a priority three weeks before the presidential elections."
Asked by reporters about the controversy, French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt did not retract Godfrain's statement.
He said Foreign Minister Herve de Charette respected Christopher as "his colleague and friend...and we ourselves have the highest appreciation for the international role of the United States".
Rummelhardt added: "We consider this affair closed."
State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns had said the comment was "a ludicrous charge made by someone who's not paid attention to what the United States has done" and "ought to be retracted."
U.S. officials say the French were upset by Christopher's trip because they saw it as trespassing on a French domain.
Christopher, who returned on Monday from his five-nation tour, said in a speech in South Africa that "Africa needs the support of all its many friends, not the exclusive patronage of a few."
